generationContext.text:
# Microsoft Azure Desktop Virtualization management client library for .NET

Microsoft Azure Virtual Desktop is a desktop and app virtualization service that runs on the cloud.

This library supports managing Microsoft Azure Desktop Virtualization resources.

This library follows the [new Azure SDK guidelines](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/general_introduction.html), and provides many core capabilities:

    - Support MSAL.NET, Azure.Identity is out of box for supporting MSAL.NET.
    - Support [OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io/) for distributed tracing.
    - HTTP pipeline with custom policies.
    - Better error-handling.
    - Support uniform telemetry across all languages.

## Getting started 

### Install the package

Install the Microsoft Azure Desktop Virtualization management library for .NET with [NuGet](https://www.nuget.org/):

```dotnetcli
dotnet add package Azure.ResourceManager.DesktopVirtualization
```

### Prerequisites

* You must have an [Microsoft Azure subscription](https://azure.microsoft.com/free/dotnet/).

### Authenticate the Client

To create an authenticated client and start interacting with Microsoft Azure resources, see the [quickstart guide here](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/doc/dev/mgmt_quickstart.md).

## Key concepts

Key concepts of the Microsoft Azure SDK for .NET can be found [here](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/dotnet_introduction.html).

## Documentation

Documentation is available to help you learn how to use this package:

- [Quickstart](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/doc/dev/mgmt_quickstart.md).
- [API References](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/?view=azure-dotnet).
- [Authentication](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/sdk/identity/Azure.Identity/README.md).

## Examples

Code samples for using the management library for .NET can be found in the following locations
- [.NET Management Library Code Samples](https://aka.ms/azuresdk-net-mgmt-samples)

## Troubleshooting

-   File an issue via [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/issues).
-   Check [previous questions](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/azure+.net) or ask new ones on Stack Overflow using Azure and .NET tags.

## Next steps

For more information about Microsoft Azure SDK, see [this website](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/).

## Contributing

For details on contributing to this repository, see the [contributing
guide][cg].

This project welcomes contributions and suggestions. Most contributions
require you to agree to a Contributor License Agreement (CLA) declaring
that you have the right to, and actually do, grant us the rights to use
your contribution. For details, visit <https://cla.microsoft.com>.

When you submit a pull request, a CLA-bot will automatically determine
whether you need to provide a CLA and decorate the PR appropriately
(for example, label, comment). Follow the instructions provided by the
bot. You'll only need to do this action once across all repositories
using our CLA.

This project has adopted the [Microsoft Open Source Code of Conduct][coc]. For
more information, see the [Code of Conduct FAQ][coc_faq] or contact
<opencode@microsoft.com> with any other questions or comments.

decisions.reason: The two bodies in the non-generated Customize partial forward to same-named overloads with a null argument. The hidden signature adapter is a handwritten convenience/compatibility surface, not an LRO implementation; the comment's historical explanation is not independently verified.

Both captured Customize partials implement the sync/async host-pool subscription adapter: extension methods call mockable methods, which insert three nulls. The same operation's two forwarding layers are grouped, with no custom page iteration claimed.

The scaling-plan extension and mockable partials visibly implement one sync/async signature adapter, and the latter inserts three null arguments; no pagination mechanics are inferred from Pageable return types.

The collection's handwritten sync/async GetAll overloads each pass three nulls plus cancellationToken to the corresponding overload; the lines establish convenience forwarding, not a handwritten pager.

The Customize partial adds a public get/set MigrationRequest with both Obsolete and EditorBrowsable(Never) annotations. This is a distinct model-member surface from the separately captured migration model; neither its serialization nor its historical cause is established.

The non-generated HostPoolResource partial supplies hidden sync/async GetScalingPlans overloads forwarding three nulls and the cancellation token; the cited bodies support the compatibility-shaped adapter rather than custom paging.

Both handwritten GetUserSessions overloads forward the supplied filter with three null arguments and cancellationToken; neither parses the filter or implements page iteration. The fixed-argument helper pattern describes the actual code without presuming legacy history.

The non-generated model partial declares a setter-bearing IList property and WirePath annotation. The code supports a handwritten member-shape override; the comment's claim about a prior generated read-only list is not independently established.

The hidden seven-argument static factory in Customize forwards to its same-named overload with null after systemData. The target overload and the historical signature change are not supplied, and the finding does not infer their behavior.

The separate ConnectionDataData factory overload visibly inserts null after systemData and forwards all seven arguments; its distinct return type/symbol warrants a separate model-factory instance without assuming the target's body.

The handwritten VirtualApplicationData factory explicitly constructs ApplicationProperties from its flat arguments and a null, then passes that model and null additionalBinaryDataProperties into VirtualApplicationData; this is supported by its cited body.

The non-generated partial defines a hidden obsolete migration class with constructors and two writable properties. These declarations form one retained model surface, not separate findings for each assignment.

The non-generated accessor creates missing Properties, returns its nested list, and on set clears and repopulates it. That is a concrete flattened model property adapter; prior API history mentioned in comments remains unverified.

The HostPoolPatch Customize partial explicitly defines a writable tag dictionary with WirePath("tags"); this changes the model member surface, while historical generated behavior in its comment is not independently shown.

The handwritten obsolete value type implements its named values, string conversion and case-insensitive equality. The proposal correctly distinguishes the raw string hash implementation from equality; no claim that their contracts are consistent is accepted.
ScalingPlanPatch adds a writable Tags dictionary with an explicit tags wire path in a non-generated partial; its separate obsolete HostPoolType member is handled under another key.

A distinct public writable nullable HostPoolType is annotated hidden and obsolete on ScalingPlanPatch. The source supports retained/deprecated model surface, not a claim about whether the service accepts its value.

The proposed explanation treats a DateTimeOffset with year zero as a usable projection. Its getter actually attempts to construct an invalid year-zero DateTimeOffset and throws; the setter still writes the two component fields. This is a handwritten but defective legacy accessor, not a working date conversion.
